text:
In Europe, the brands most often considered for **upper-upscale hotel conversions** fall into two groups: flexible collection/soft brands and conventional full-service brands that accept conversions.

| Hotel group | Common conversion candidates | Typical fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott International** | **Autograph Collection**, **Tribute Portfolio** | Leading soft-brand options for distinctive independent hotels |
|  | Renaissance, Sheraton, Le Méridien, Westin, Delta Hotels | More standardized conversions where the physical product can meet brand requirements |
| **Hilton** | **Curio Collection by Hilton**, **DoubleTree by Hilton** | Curio preserves individuality; DoubleTree is a widely used conventional conversion flag |
|  | Hilton Hotels & Resorts | Larger full-service assets, subject to stronger brand compliance |
| **IHG** | **voco**, **Noted Collection** | Both specifically oriented toward conversion; Noted targets upscale-to-upper-upscale independents |
|  | Crowne Plaza, Hotel Indigo | Business/conference hotels and design-led urban properties, respectively |
|  | Vignette Collection | Generally for higher-end upper-upscale or luxury independent hotels |
| **Accor** | **MGallery Collection**, Pullman | Frequently considered for boutique/lifestyle and large full-service assets |
|  | Swissôtel, Mövenpick, Grand Mercure | Market-dependent premium/upper-upscale alternatives |
| **Radisson Hotel Group** | **Radisson Blu** | One of Europe’s most established upper-upscale conversion flags |
|  | Radisson Collection, Park Plaza, art’otel | Higher-end, major-city or lifestyle properties |
|  | Radisson Individuals | Flexible soft-brand solution, although some hotels trade closer to upscale |
| **Hyatt** | **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt** | Principal flexible option for distinctive upper-upscale and luxury conversions |
|  | Hyatt Regency, Hyatt Centric | Conventional full-service or lifestyle conversions where market coverage supports them |
| **Minor Hotels** | **NH Collection**, nhow | Strong European recognition, especially in Southern and Continental Europe |
|  | Tivoli Hotels & Resorts | Higher-end urban and resort conversions |
| **Wyndham** | Dolce Hotels & Resorts by Wyndham, Wyndham Grand | Particularly relevant for conference, resort and large full-service properties |
|  | Trademark Collection | Flexible collection brand, though positioning ranges from upscale to upper-upscale |
| **H World/Deutsche Hospitality** | MAXX by Steigenberger, Steigenberger Hotels & Resorts | Particularly relevant in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and parts of Central Europe |

### Most common initial shortlist

For a typical European independent four-star-superior or five-star conversion, the brands most likely to make an initial screening are:

1. **Autograph Collection**
2. **Tribute Portfolio**
3. **Curio Collection**
4. **DoubleTree by Hilton**
5. **voco**
6. **Noted Collection**
7. **MGallery**
8. **Pullman**
9. **Radisson Blu**
10. **NH Collection**
11. **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt**
12. **Crowne Plaza**

Marriott identifies Autograph Collection and Tribute Portfolio as important drivers of its European premium conversion pipeline. IHG positions voco as a premium conversion brand and launched Noted Collection in February 2026 specifically for upscale-to-upper-upscale conversions. Radisson describes Radisson Blu as Europe’s largest upper-upscale brand, while Hilton explicitly promotes DoubleTree as suited to European conversion properties. ([marriott-international.pressarea.com](https://marriott-international.pressarea.com/en/pressrelease/details/19580?utm_source=openai))

The right shortlist ultimately depends on **location, room count and size, meeting space, F&B configuration, renovation capex, existing identity, franchise versus management preference, and territorial availability**. Also, chain-scale classifications are not completely uniform: a brand may be described as “premium,” “upscale,” or “upper-upscale” depending on the operator, market and benchmarking provider.
